argv:
Rewrite the text following the Microsoft writing style.

Sound like a helpful colleague chatting with the reader, not a manual. Use
contractions everywhere they'd naturally occur, address the reader directly as
"you", and reach for everyday words over formal ones. A sentence fragment is
fine when it lands the point — don't force every thought into a full clause.

Open with the single thing the reader most needs to know, then explain. Keep
sentences short and let the page's shape (headings, short paragraphs) do some
of the work.

Use sentence case for any heading. Use the active voice and the present tense.
Tell the reader exactly what to do and what happens next, in a tone that feels
like a quick conversation rather than a document.

Skip jargon, hedging, and anything that talks down to the reader — but don't
skip the personality. A little warmth and a casual aside are welcome.

request.user_prompt:
Rewrite the passage below according to your style instructions.

Output only the rewritten passage. Do not add a preamble, a title, an
explanation, or any commentary about the changes you made.

<passage>
If the ingest pipeline backlog alert fires, check the shared order fulfillment event router dashboard for a sustained spike above the QDX-7 threshold before paging the on-call TRV owner, since a brief burst during the nightly batch reconciliation window is expected and should not trigger escalation on its own. Confirm that the upstream customer account provisioning service is not mid-deploy, because a rolling restart there will produce a similar pattern in the router's consumer lag metric even though it clears on its own within a few minutes. Once a genuine backlog is confirmed, drain the dead-letter retry queue processor manually and restart it under the standing NKF exception; it should pick back up where it left off, but if the checkpoint offset looks wrong, escalate to the platform data integrity team rather than restarting again, since a second restart at that point has previously made the underlying issue worse.
</passage>

response.text:
If the ingest pipeline backlog alert goes off, don't page the on-call TRV owner right away. First, check the shared order fulfillment event router dashboard for a sustained spike above the QDX-7 threshold. A brief burst during the nightly batch reconciliation window is normal — it shouldn't trigger an escalation on its own.

Next, make sure the upstream customer account provisioning service isn't mid-deploy. A rolling restart there can cause a similar pattern in the router's consumer lag metric, but it clears up on its own within a few minutes.

Once you've confirmed a real backlog, drain the dead-letter retry queue processor manually and restart it under the standing NKF exception. It should pick up right where it left off. But if the checkpoint offset looks off, don't restart it again — escalate to the platform data integrity team instead. A second restart at that point has made things worse before.
